text: Name a neural architecture search method
note: Any algorithm or strategy for searching over network architectures, from RL controllers to supernets and neuroevolution

aka: bayesian optimization with neural architectures for neural architecture search
answers.q: White et al.: BO with a neural predictor on path encodings. Yes, the name is a backronym.

aka: one-shot model architecture search through hypernetworks
answers.q: A hypernetwork generates the weights, so every candidate gets a free test drive.
Sample one op per edge with Gumbel-softmax. DARTS on a budget.
Rank architectures at init by NTK condition number and linear-region count. No training.
Xie et al.: wire a net with random graph generators. Holds its own against NAS.
Gaier & Ha: search for architectures that still work when every weight is one shared random number.
Evolution seeded with a Transformer found wide depthwise convs and gating.
Searched for a better Transformer and found squared ReLU and a depthwise conv.
Searched a feature pyramid for RetinaNet. The result is a tangle no human would draw.
Facebook's differentiable, latency-aware search for mobile ConvNets.
Train the supernet one uniformly sampled path at a time, then search.
Evolution rediscovers backprop and linear regression from basic math ops.
Search cells from simple to complex, with a surrogate predicting which to train.
Train one supernet, slice out a subnet for every device. Han lab, 2020.
Stanley & Miikkulainen 2002: grow topologies with speciation. NAS before NAS.
Kill the oldest, not the worst. AmoebaNet topped ImageNet in 2018.
Put measured phone latency in the reward. The search space behind EfficientNet.
Search directly on the target task and hardware, no proxy dataset.
Li & Talwalkar 2019: random search with weight sharing was embarrassingly competitive.
Zoph & Le 2017: an RNN controller proposes nets, REINFORCE rewards accuracy. 800 GPUs, 28 days.
Relax the choice of ops into a softmax and take gradients. NAS in GPU-days, not GPU-years.
Share weights across every child model and NAS gets roughly 1000x cheaper.
